hero.title: Debt collection, reimagined.
hero.subtitle: GORKA is a modern debt collection platform that brings team workflows, communication integrations, and AI-assisted productivity together—with a local-first approach to protecting your debtor data.
hero.subtext: Get the convenience of modern software, keep operational data under your organization's control, and give your team tools to work smarter. Designed for collection agencies and lenders ready to modernize their operations.

features.title: Built for modern collections, designed for compliance

items.headline: Collection software, without the IT burden
items.subheadline: SaaS convenience for modern collection teams.
items.body: Get started with a straightforward onboarding process, manage your team, and support distributed work. GORKA is designed to help growing collection businesses scale without the complexity and infrastructure traditionally associated with large business systems.

items.headline: Cloud convenience. Local data control.
items.subheadline: Designed to protect your most sensitive business data.
items.body: GORKA keeps operational debtor data on your organization's devices and synchronizes selected records between authorized devices through encryption. Its central platform is designed to coordinate your service without decrypting your debtor records.

items.headline: Less routine. More informed action.
items.subheadline: A practical AI Copilot, with people in control.
items.body: Help your team work through routine tasks with AI-assisted recommendations and email drafts. Your agents review the suggestions, check the facts, and decide what to do. GORKA's AI foundation is designed to evolve as new, responsible business-assistance capabilities are developed.

items.headline: Modern capabilities. A sensible price.
items.body: Advanced collection software should be within reach of smaller teams, not only large institutions. GORKA aims to combine modern capabilities with accessible pricing, so you can invest in better workflows without taking on the cost and complexity of a heavyweight IT system.

items.headline: One platform. A smarter way to collect.
items.body: GORKA brings local-first data architecture, encrypted synchronization, team workflows, communication integrations, and AI-assisted productivity into one collection platform. Instead of choosing between convenience and control, your organization gets a foundation designed around both.

security.description: GORKA uses a local-first architecture — your data never leaves your infrastructure unless you choose to use a cloud provider.
security.detail: For banks and agencies handling sensitive debtor information, this means full control over compliance, security, and data sovereignty.

faq.title: Questions answered
faq.intro: GORKA helps collection teams organize their work, coordinate across devices, and make more informed decisions—while keeping control of their data in their own hands. Here are answers to the questions we think matter most.

items.question: What is GORKA?
items.answer: GORKA is a debt collection platform designed to help collection agencies and lenders manage overdue accounts, coordinate collection teams, record actions and communications, and work more efficiently. It combines local data storage, team collaboration, communication integrations, and AI-assisted recommendations in one platform.

items.question: Who is GORKA built for?
items.answer: GORKA is designed primarily for collection agencies and small lenders that manage overdue accounts with a team of agents. Its architecture is intended to support organizations that want better coordination and visibility without giving up control of their data.

items.question: What makes GORKA different from other debt collection software?
items.answer: GORKA is built around a local-first approach. Instead of relying on a central cloud database containing all your debtor information, its applications keep operational data on your organization's devices and synchronize selected information between authorized devices using encrypted event-based synchronization. GORKA also brings collection workflows, team collaboration, external communication integrations, and AI-assisted recommendations together in a privacy-conscious design.

items.question: Is GORKA suitable for a small agency, or is it only for large organizations?
items.answer: GORKA is intended to serve collection teams of different sizes, starting with collection agencies and smaller lenders. You can begin with your own workflow and evaluate whether the available features meet your team's operational needs before expanding.

items.question: Does GORKA replace my existing collection process?
items.answer: GORKA is designed to support and improve your collection workflow, not to remove your team's judgment. Your organization remains responsible for its collection policies, decisions, and communications.

items.question: Where is my data stored?
items.answer: GORKA's Client and Agent applications maintain operational data locally on your organization's devices. Selected information can synchronize between authorized devices through encrypted event-based synchronization. GORKA's central Control Plane supports functions such as authentication, organization and device management, and service coordination. It is not designed to store or decrypt your debtor records.

items.question: Can GORKA's central servers read my debtor data?
items.answer: GORKA's architecture is designed so the central Control Plane cannot decrypt your locally stored debtor data or read debtor information carried through the encrypted synchronization channel. This boundary is a core architectural principle. However, it does not mean that every piece of information involved in every feature stays local: external services may receive data when you choose to use them.

items.question: Does GORKA send my debtor data to the cloud?
items.answer: Not as a complete, centrally stored debtor database. GORKA is designed to keep operational debtor data on your organization's devices and synchronize selected records in encrypted form. Some features involve external services. For example, sending an email requires communicating with an email provider, and using an external AI provider involves sending an approved request to that provider. The information shared depends on the feature and its configuration.

items.question: Is my data encrypted?
items.answer: GORKA uses encryption for local database protection and for synchronization between authorized devices. Its synchronization design uses authenticated encryption to protect event data in transit. Encryption is one layer of security, not a guarantee against every threat. Device security, account access, credential handling, backups, and your organization's operating practices also matter.

items.question: What happens if an employee leaves my organization?
items.answer: Access should be managed through your organization's user and device administration processes. You should review and revoke access where supported when an employee leaves. Important limitation: the current MVP does not provide per-machine cryptographic identity, cryptographic device revocation, or organization-key rotation. Removing an account or device should therefore not be assumed to invalidate copies of encryption keys or data that the device already holds. Organizations should establish appropriate offboarding and device-security procedures.

items.question: Can GORKA access my data without my permission?
items.answer: GORKA's architecture is designed to prevent the central Control Plane from decrypting local debtor records. Access to the applications and their data still depends on device security, authentication, user permissions, and who has access to the organization's encryption key. You should protect user credentials, secure your devices, and limit access to authorized personnel.

items.question: What happens if a device is lost or damaged?
items.answer: A lost or damaged device can make locally stored information unavailable. Other authorized devices may have synchronized copies of eligible records, but synchronization is not a substitute for a verified backup. Your organization should maintain a backup and recovery procedure appropriate to its operational and legal requirements.

items.question: Does GORKA guarantee compliance with debt collection and privacy laws?
items.answer: No software can guarantee compliance in every jurisdiction or business situation. GORKA can support more organized workflows and controlled communications, but your organization remains responsible for applicable debt collection, privacy, consumer protection, recordkeeping, and communications requirements. You should review your intended use of GORKA with qualified legal or compliance advisers in the jurisdictions where you operate.

items.question: How do I load my accounts into GORKA?
items.answer: The planned onboarding workflow starts with importing a CSV file. GORKA's import experience is intended to help identify the columns in your file so you do not have to prepare every file against a rigid template. Before importing real customer data, review the supported fields and validate the import with a small sample. Other file formats and direct integrations may be introduced as the product develops.

items.question: Can I import data from my existing collection system?
items.answer: You can start with supported CSV exports from your existing system. Whether a direct connection is available depends on the source system and the integrations supported by GORKA. If you rely on a specific database, CRM, loan management system, or collection platform, discuss the required import fields and migration process with us before committing to a migration.

items.question: Can my team work together across multiple devices?
items.answer: Yes. GORKA's Client and Agent applications are designed to coordinate through encrypted event-based synchronization. Selected records can be shared between authorized devices without synchronizing the entire local database. Not every data category is synchronized. For example, debts and documents are local-only in the current synchronization scope, while eligible debtor records, actions, and communication logs can synchronize. Plan your workflow around these boundaries.

items.question: What happens when a device is offline?
items.answer: Local-first architecture is intended to let the applications work with locally available data without depending on a central database for every operation. Synchronization can resume when the necessary connections are available. However, information created on one device may not be available on another until it synchronizes. Your team should understand which records are local-only and how to recognize synchronization status.

items.question: Can I control what each employee can access?
items.answer: GORKA supports organization and user management, with roles that distinguish owners, clients, and agents. Access should be configured according to each person's responsibilities. Do not assume that every feature supports fine-grained permissions, branch-level restrictions, or assignment-only visibility. Confirm the exact access controls available in your version before relying on them for a particular workflow.

items.question: What does the GORKA AI Copilot do?
items.answer: The AI Copilot is designed to assist collection agents by generating recommendations and drafting email messages using approved context from the local application. It is an assistant for your team—not an autonomous collection agent. Your staff remain responsible for reviewing recommendations, checking facts, and deciding what to do.

items.question: Does the AI send messages automatically?
items.answer: No. The current Copilot workflow is designed around human review and approval. It does not independently send messages without the required user action. Before sending, GORKA applies relevant validation and compliance checks. A draft that fails the applicable checks should not be sent through the Copilot workflow.

items.question: Does the AI see all my debtor information?
items.answer: No. The Copilot is designed to use an allowlist of approved context rather than automatically sending an entire debtor record to an AI provider. The system is designed to exclude direct identifiers and other unapproved sensitive details from AI context. The actual information sent depends on the configured feature and provider request, so organizations should review their AI configuration and provider terms before enabling it.

items.question: Which AI provider does GORKA use?
items.answer: The Copilot architecture supports configured external AI providers, including Gemini and compatible providers using an OpenAI-style API. Availability depends on the current release and configuration. The provider processes the AI request outside GORKA. Review the provider's data handling, retention, and privacy terms before using it with business data.

items.question: Can the AI make mistakes?
items.answer: Yes. AI-generated recommendations and messages can be incomplete, misleading, or factually incorrect. GORKA's Copilot workflow includes validation intended to catch certain problems, but no automated check can guarantee that every recommendation is correct. Agents should verify important facts, review the proposed wording, and follow organizational policies before acting on a recommendation.

items.question: Does GORKA use AI to decide which debtors deserve collection action?
items.answer: The Copilot is designed to support recommendations and drafting, not to replace human judgment with autonomous collection decisions. Its current scope should not be confused with an unrestricted predictive scoring system or a system that independently decides whom to pursue. Your organization remains responsible for fair, lawful, and appropriate collection practices.

items.question: Can I send emails or text messages from GORKA?
items.answer: GORKA's connector architecture supports external communication services, including email and SMS providers. The services available to you depend on the current release, your configuration, and your provider credentials. Using an external provider means the relevant message content and delivery information must be shared with that provider to perform the requested service.

items.question: Do I need my own provider accounts and credentials?
items.answer: It depends on the integration. Some supported services use a managed-provider model, while others use a bring-your-own-provider arrangement in which your organization supplies its own credentials. The applicable requirements, costs, and setup steps should be checked for each connector before enabling it.

items.question: Does GORKA store my communication-provider passwords or API keys in its cloud?
items.answer: GORKA's architecture is designed to keep provider credentials out of the central Control Plane. Credentials for supported bring-your-own-provider integrations are stored locally in the protected application database and may be synchronized in encrypted form to authorized devices that need them. You remain responsible for protecting your provider accounts and following the provider's credential-management guidance.

items.question: How much does GORKA cost?
items.answer: GORKA offers a free plan to help organizations get started. Professional is intended for growing teams, while Enterprise pricing is tailored to organizational needs. Plan availability, feature limits, and current prices are listed on the Pricing page. External provider charges—such as email, SMS, voice, or AI usage—may be separate from your GORKA subscription.

items.question: What do I need to get started?
items.answer: You can begin by creating an account and verifying your email. The current onboarding flow is designed around downloading the GORKA Client application for Windows, signing in, completing initial setup, and importing your first supported data file. You will need appropriate access to the device where you install the application and authorization to use the data you import.

items.question: Does GORKA work on Mac, Linux, or mobile devices?
items.answer: The current onboarding and installation workflow is focused on Windows desktop applications. Do not assume that Mac, Linux, or mobile versions are available unless they are explicitly listed on the website.

items.question: Can I try GORKA before paying?
items.answer: GORKA has a free plan intended to let prospective customers start evaluating the platform. Check the Pricing page for the current limits and included features. For an evaluation, use a small, controlled sample of data and verify that the available workflows fit your requirements before migrating production records.

items.question: How do I get help choosing the right setup?
items.answer: If you are unsure whether GORKA fits your collection process, book a demo or contact the team. We can discuss your team size, current data sources, communication providers, security requirements, and onboarding needs. We recommend resolving important requirements—especially access control, data recovery, compliance, and integrations—before moving production data into a new system.

closing.title: Still have questions?
closing.body: Tell us about your collection workflow and what you need to improve. We can help you evaluate whether GORKA is the right fit for your organization.

dataControl.title: Your data shouldn't have to live in someone else's cloud.
dataControl.intro: Traditional cloud software often relies on a central database containing customer records. GORKA takes a different architectural approach.
dataControl.body: Your operational debtor data is maintained locally by GORKA's applications on your organization's devices. Selected records synchronize between authorized devices through encrypted event-based synchronization, while the central Control Plane coordinates essential platform services without being designed to decrypt your debtor records.
dataControl.whatThisMeans: What this means for your business
dataControl.point1Desc: Your operational debtor records are not designed to reside in a central GORKA debtor database.
dataControl.point2Desc: Selected information can synchronize between authorized Client and Agent devices.
dataControl.point3Desc: Your core debtor records are separated architecturally from the central services that support the platform.
dataControl.point4Desc: You can evaluate where data lives, which information synchronizes, and what external services receive before adopting a workflow.
dataControl.conclusion: GORKA combines the convenience of a modern software service with an architecture designed around data control.
dataControl.cta: Discover how GORKA protects your data

aiVision.eyebrow: INTELLIGENCE THAT GROWS WITH YOUR BUSINESS
aiVision.title: More than automation. A smarter way to work.
aiVision.intro: Collection teams handle repetitive tasks, scattered information, and constant decisions about what to do next. GORKA's AI Copilot is designed to help reduce that burden—while keeping your people in control.
aiVision.todayDesc: The current Copilot foundation supports AI-assisted recommendations and email drafting using approved context. Agents review suggestions, verify important facts, and decide what action to take.
aiVision.directionTitle: The direction: intelligence built around your business
aiVision.directionDesc: Our longer-term vision is to develop more capable search, analysis, and decision-support tools grounded in the information and experience of each customer's own business. As the platform evolves, this could include more intelligent ways to find relevant information across connected data sources, identify patterns, and support operational decisions using authentic business data—not generic demonstrations or purchased datasets presented as your own experience.
aiVision.privacyTitle: Privacy remains part of the design.
aiVision.privacyDesc: Any future analytical or machine-learning capabilities must be designed with clear customer control, defined data boundaries, and appropriate safeguards. Using customer data for model training or learning is not an automatic part of the current MVP.

whyGorka.title: Built for the realities of modern debt collection.
whyGorka.intro: Your collection operation shouldn't have to choose between convenience, data control, useful technology, and cost. GORKA brings these priorities together in one platform.
whyGorka.point1Desc: A SaaS-style experience designed to simplify onboarding, team coordination, and growth—without requiring every customer to build and maintain a heavyweight IT environment.
whyGorka.point2Desc: A connector-based architecture for supported communication and AI providers, giving your team a more unified way to access essential services instead of managing every integration as a separate project.
whyGorka.point3Desc: Local-first operational data and encrypted synchronization are architectural decisions, not just another security feature added to a conventional centralized database.
whyGorka.point4Desc: Start with recommendations and email drafting. Build toward more capable assistance and business intelligence as the product and its safeguards mature.
whyGorka.point5Desc: Modern collection software should not be out of reach for growing agencies. GORKA aims to deliver meaningful capabilities at a more accessible price point.
whyGorka.conclusion: GORKA brings the pieces together: modern delivery, local data control, connected services, and AI-assisted work—designed specifically around collection operations.
